title: Small enough to serve
hook: the bravest monkey in the army chooses to be the size of a cat, and why Hindus see him as the model servant
carry: dasya: serve without needing to be seen

segments.voice: Yesterday: three meetings, answered with courtesy, wit and force, and your line: pray to Hanuman for wisdom, not only strength.

Hanuman stands on a hilltop at the edge of the sea, and in front of him is Lanka. A city on a mountain, ringed with golden walls, moats full of water, guarded gates, towers that seem to touch the clouds. Banners. Gardens. It is breathtaking, and it is very obviously a fortress. The monkey who just crossed an ocean in one leap stands still and thinks.
screen: `A CITY ON A MOUNTAIN.` → `GOLDEN WALLS, GUARDED GATES.` → `HANUMAN STANDS STILL.`

segments.voice: What Hanuman thinks about isn't how strong he is. It's how easily he could ruin everything. Valmiki lets us hear him reason. Rakshasas guard this city everywhere. If I'm seen in my own form, there'll be a fight, Ravana will be warned, and Sita may be put in greater danger. A messenger who shows off can wreck the very thing he was sent to do. So his plan is the opposite of a hero's entrance. He'll wait for night, make himself as small as a cat, and slip in unseen. The sun goes down. He shrinks and makes for the city, and as he goes, the moon rises, Valmiki says, like a swan gliding on a lake. The greatest leaper in the story chooses to be small, because the work is Rama's, not his. Hindu tradition has a name for this. Among the ways of loving God, the Bhagavata Purana lists dasya, devotion as service, and Hanuman is its great example: the servant who wants Rama's work done, not his own name shouted. It's why, in the Ram Darbar, the picture of Rama's court found in so many family shrines, the mightiest figure is the one kneeling at Rama's feet, hands folded. The Hanuman Chalisa sings this side of him too: he took a tiny form to appear before Sita.
screen: `HOW EASILY HE COULD RUIN IT.` · `AS SMALL AS A CAT, BY NIGHT.` · `DASYA: LOVE AS SERVICE.` · then, large: `KNEELING AT RAMA'S FEET.`

segments.voice: Fold your hands the way Hanuman does in the Ram Darbar. If you pray, offer one ordinary piece of today's work, a chore, homework, a shift, to God, with Rama's name or the name you use. If you don't pray, choose one task you'll do today for someone else without mentioning it. Breathe, and let it be enough that it gets done.
Lanka, Ravana's golden island city, which Hanuman enters by night, as small as a cat, because the work matters more than being seen.
Your line: dasya, serve without needing to be seen. Someone at the gate is about to notice him anyway. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 612 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A CITY FULL OF MUSIC.`
